relationships.subject: galcanezumab
relationships.evidence_quote: galcanezumab, a humanized monoclonal antibody targeting calcitonin gene-related peptide (CGRP), received an FDA approval for the prevention of episodic CH.

relationships.subject: galcanezumab
relationships.evidence_quote: the galcanezumab treatment group experienced a significant reduction in weekly attack frequency compared to the placebo group.

relationships.subject: galcanezumab
relationships.evidence_quote: a phase 3, randomized, placebo-controlled study found that galcanezumab was not effective in reducing the frequency of attacks in patients with cCH compared to placebo over a 3-month double-blind treatment period.

relationships.subject: high-flow oxygen
relationships.evidence_quote: The mechanism underlying the efficacy of high-flow oxygen in CH is thought to involve the inhibition of trigeminal nerve activation and subsequent reduction of neurogenic inflammation.

relationships.subject: verapamil
relationships.evidence_quote: Studies have shown that verapamil treatment significantly reduces attack frequency in patients with both episodic and chronic CH.

key_findings: Narrative review of Taiwan CH management: high-flow oxygen and triptan nasal spray acutely, verapamil first-line prevention.
Galcanezumab reduced attacks in episodic CH but failed in chronic CH.
